page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 12 physical cores and 12 vCPUs with shared CPU allocation and a single thread per core. Memory capacity is set at 128.0 GB, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. The server is equipped with a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 24 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 4036.38 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 42.27 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 47554.45 and a PassMark CPU score of 36792.38. Memory performance is strong for large-block read-only operations at 254.5 GB/sec, while write operations and small-block reads remain in the average tier. For AI workloads, the NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier text generation speeds of 345.71 tokens/sec for a small 135M LLM model, though prompt processing for the same model is average at 1877.79 tokens/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of over 10 GB per core paired with a dedicated 24 GB GPU offers a specialized hardware profile for memory-intensive acceleration tasks. However, the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage represent key tradeoffs for workloads requiring dedicated compute cycles or high-speed local disk I/O. This server is suited for lightweight LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science jobs, and GPU-accelerated rendering or simulation tasks where high memory capacity and single-core efficiency are prioritized over multi-core density.
